text:
A: Hi.
B: Alright.
A: I am Jurgita.
B: Callum.
A: Where you are?
B: Swindon.
A: Okay. Wakefield.
B: Right.
A: You work?
B: Not at the minute. Redundancy, from a sports shop. I was assistant manager. Looking for warehouse stuff now, off the M4.
A: My husband works in warehouse. Forklift. Off M62.
B: Yeah? Does he like it?
A: He likes money. Nights pay more, so he does nights, and I do days, and we see each other on Sunday, maybe. And always they change his shifts also, like my rota. Last week his manager says, you work Saturday, and he says, I have plans, and manager says, plans are not my problem. Is same in care home. I am senior care assistant, twelve-hour days, and they put rota on the board and nobody asks you nothing.
B: That's what I'm trying to avoid really. Regular rota. No weekend lates.
A: Good luck. Everybody says regular rota. Is never regular.
B: Yeah. Probably.
A: Yes.
B: I used to do the rotas at the shop. I wasn't very good at it, to be honest. Always last minute.
A: So you are the one who changes rota without asking.
B: Ha. Yeah, sort of. Sorry.
A: Is okay. You are not my manager.
B: No.
A: You have PlayStation, in photo. Darius also. He plays football game until two in the morning, then he is mardy all day.
B: Yeah, I do that. EA FC. Jess, my girlfriend, says the same.
A: Is good game?
B: It's alright. Same every year really, they just change the kits. You still buy it though.
A: Darius watches basketball also. Lithuanian league and NBA. I sit and look at phone.
B: I'm more football. Swindon Town. They're rubbish though.
A: Okay.
B: Yeah. That's it really.
A: Sports shop, you get discount?
B: Yeah, staff discount. Thirty percent on trainers. Miss that, actually.
A: Thirty percent is good. I buy everything in sale. TK Maxx, Vinted. I got Michael Kors bag for forty pound.
B: Fair play.
A: Proper bargain. What you will do with redundancy money?
B: Erm, bills mostly. Jess pays most of them at the minute, so.
A: Yes. Is hard when one person pays.
B: Yeah.
A: Darius and me, we save for house deposit. Eight years we save. Every time, something. Car, holiday, MOT.
B: Jess keeps going on about buying a place.
A: Then you need job with no—
